A muscle fibre relaxes when its motor neuron stops firing, so acetylcholine is cleared from the neuromuscular junction and the fibre is no longer excited. SERCA then pumps calcium back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and tropomyosin re-blocks the actin binding sites. Neither option in the team note is correct: oxygen shortage causes fatigue or cramp rather than relaxation, and muscle fibres have no mechanism that makes them go slack when the nerve signal is strong.

CONFIDENCE: 80
